描述_ZN: Zhou Wen You Da Zhuang Yan Temple Statue", ink on paper, mounted on a vertical scroll, 116 cm in length and 55 cm in width. The ink and paper are from the late Qing to early Republican period. No inscription seal.　　According to the form of this topography, the original stone is known to be a statue monument. The upper part of the monument is carved with a Buddha and two bodhisattvas in simple form, with simple and ancient clothing patterns.　　At the bottom right of the statue, three lines of inscriptions are engraved on the statue, with a boundary grid, with about 16 characters in a row, totaling 47 characters. The text says: "In the second year of Yongding, on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh month in the autumn of the year wuyin, Zhou Wenyu was honored to create an area of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life for all the surnames of the disciples of all sentient beings at the Grand Chuang Yen Temple, and all the surnames of the disciples made offerings with one heart." 　　At the bottom left of the Buddha statue, there are four columns with 20 names of supporters inscribed in the upper and lower Yang, with a boundary grid. The narrow space above the first, second, and third columns is inscribed horizontally and sharply with the words "Disciples of all surnames", "One heart to offer", and "Buddha of Immeasurable Life", totaling 12 characters.　　"Yongding" was the year name of Chen Baxian, the founding emperor of the Southern Chen Dynasty. The second year of Yongding was 558 AD. The Chen dynasty was only 33 years old, and it was a period of great social change, so there are very few jinshi documents in circulation. This stone is well engraved, well preserved, and has never been recorded, so it can be called a curiosity. The only difference is that the calligraphic style on it is the same as that of the Cuanbaozi Monument, which was erected in Qujing, Yunnan Province, in the fourth year of the Eastern Jin Dynasty (405), which is incomprehensible.
